subject: Private deployment — amendment to clarify infra responsibility and availability commitments
messages:
From: James O'Connor <james.oconnor@zenith.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.ai>
Cc: IT Security <itsecurity@zenith.com>, Procurement <procurement@zenith.com>
Date: Thu, 12 Nov 2026 09:12:00 +0000
Subject: Request: SLA alignment for private deployment

Hi Mina,

Thanks again for the demo last week. We're close to greenlighting the Redwood Private deployment into our EU data centers (details attached) but our legal and security teams have raised a couple of items around the SLA language for on-prem / customer-controlled infra. Specifically:

- Zenith controls networking, host lifecycle, and storage for the cluster; we need the contract to explicitly reflect that host-level outages (power/network hardware at our DC) should be carved out from Redwood uptime credits.
- We also need clarity on latency commitments and whether Redwood will accept any exceptions when the customer-run layer (load balancers, network fabric) is the likely root cause.
- What monitoring and logs will Redwood require from us to investigate incidents and to determine whether an outage is within Redwood's responsibility?

Can you provide a proposed amendment or redline we can take to our security and procurement teams? Ideally, we want a short, clear clause that protects both sides and spells out required observability.

Attached: zenith-deployment-outline.pdf

Thanks,
James
James O'Connor
Head of Platform Engineering, Zenith Financial
From: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.ai>
To: James O'Connor <james.oconnor@zenith.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>, Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 13 Nov 2026 11:05:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Request: SLA alignment for private deployment

James —

Appreciate the clear ask and the deployment outline. You're right that Private (customer-hosted) deployments are a shared-responsibility model: Redwood's SLA covers the inference control plane and the software components we manage; it does not, by default, cover customer-managed networking or hardware.

That said, we can (and often do) draft a short amendment that:
- Defines "Redwood-managed components" vs "Customer-managed infrastructure"
- Explicitly excludes host/network hardware failures from Redwood uptime credits
- Provides an availability commitment for the Redwood service layer when the customer meets specific observability requirements (see below)

To move fast, I'll draft proposed redline language and loop in Legal and Solutions. Can we schedule a 30-minute sync next week with your IT Security folks so we can agree on the minimum telemetry set?

I'll attach a first-pass amendment and a short monitoring checklist.

Regards,
Mina Haddad
Director, Customer Solutions — Redwood Inference
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 14 Nov 2026 08:30:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Request: SLA alignment for private deployment

Putting a commercial lens on this: Zenith is a strategic EU deal — worth our sales motion to be flexible. Proposal ideas:

- Offer a 99.0% availability commitment for Redwood-managed service components running in the customer's VPC, contingent on Zenith providing the monitoring and access described below.
- Explicit carveout language for customer infra (power/network/hypervisor).
- Include an incident escalation SLA (e.g., P1 response within 1 hour, remediation plan within 4 hours) for Redwood-managed failures.
- As a gesture, offer a one-time onboarding credit (discounted Dedicated hours) if they sign the amendment within 30 days.

This preserves our operational commitments while acknowledging the shared responsibility. Legal to weigh in on wording and indemnities.

- Rishi
VP, Sales Operations
From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>, Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 16 Nov 2026 13:10:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Request: SLA alignment for private deployment

Team —

Attached is a draft amendment with suggested language. Key elements included:

1) Definitions:
   - "Redwood Service" = inference runtime, orchestrator, control-plane components we install/operate.
   - "Customer Infrastructure" = anything the customer owns/operates (hosts, switches, load balancers, storage network).

2) Exclusions:
   - Redwood credits are not payable for incidents caused solely by Customer Infrastructure (examples listed).

3) Contingent Availability Commitment:
   - Redwood will commit to 99.0% availability for the Redwood Service when Customer provides:
     a) 7x24 access to node-level health endpoints and per-node agent metrics (format listed in monitoring spec).
     b) Load balancer request logs (time-synced to UTC) for a rolling 90-day window.
     c) A documented maintenance calendar for scheduled host/network work.

4) Investigation & Evidence:
   - Both parties agree to share logs, packet captures (where feasible), and traceroutes for root cause analysis.

5) Remedies:
   - Limited credits tied to measured downtime of Redwood Service only; no liability for customer infra.

I've attached proposed-sla-amendment.docx and a monitoring checklist (sla-monitoring-specs.txt). Please review — we should be conservative on indemnity language.

Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Contracts — Redwood Inference
From: Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwood.ai>
To: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 17 Nov 2026 10:45:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Request: SLA alignment for private deployment

Quick technical note to support the monitoring checklist:

- Minimum telemetry we need from Zenith: per-node /health, /metrics (Prometheus exposition format), NGINX access + error logs with request_id, and per-process memory/CPU snapshots at 1m granularity.
- Latency SLO: we can commit to a 95th percentile tail for Redwood-managed path (examples: model inference time) but end-to-end client latency can be affected by customer LB and network. Recommend wording: "Redwood measures latency for requests received by its ingress; latency SLOs apply to the Redwood-managed execution path only."

Example snippet for a node health check response we expect:

{
  "node": "node-17",
  "status": "ok",
  "kv_cache": "warm",
  "uptime_seconds": 129382
}

If Zenith can host a small metrics-forwarder (collectd/Prometheus node exporter) and grant read-only access to the metrics endpoint, we can automate health checks and reduce incident triage time.

- Diego
Principal Solutions Engineer
From: James O'Connor <james.oconnor@zenith.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.ai>
Cc: IT Security <itsecurity@zenith.com>, Procurement <procurement@zenith.com>
Date: Fri, 20 Nov 2026 14:22:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Request: SLA alignment for private deployment

Mina —

Thanks for the quick turnaround and the proposed language. We reviewed the amendment internally (small edits from our side limited to maintenance-window notice periods) and are comfortable signing if Redwood can accept the contingent availability clause (99.0% for Redwood-managed components) tied to the monitoring checklist.

I've attached the signed DocuSign envelope (docusign-zenith-sla.pdf) and linked the envelope above. Next steps from our side: we will provision a metrics-forwarder and share read-only endpoints with your SREs next week. Can you confirm who on the Redwood side will be our onboarding SRE and where we should open the SUP ticket?

Regards,
James
Head of Platform Engineering, Zenith Financial
